messages.subject: Light analysis with GGIR
parts:
Hi everybody,

Perhaps you can help me with this question: I am exploring the light analysis performed by GGIR, but I can't find a way for GGIR to output the average light activity within a specific time window.

For example, suppose I want to obtain the light intensity from 19:00 to 21:00 for each day of a participant. Is this possible? I can't figure out which parameter to modify in part 5

thanks in advance!!

messages.author: 4b9dc262ec278dc5
messages.subject: Re: Light analysis with GGIR
parts:

Please have a look at parameter  LUX_day_segments.

Best,
Jairo

Hi Jiro,

I used it but.. when I check the results, it seems to still consider the entire day instead of the specified time range. My goal is to calculate light exposure metrics within a specific time window, for example, from 20:00 to 00:00. 

  Here is an example of the output I am getting:
LUX_max_day    LUX_mean_day    LUX_mean_spt    LUX_mean_day_mvpa    LUX_min_0_100_day
19748.3                    4568.4                                   0               14188                                    379

Here is my code:


# ggir ----
GGIR::GGIR(
  mode=c(1,2,3,4,5)
  datadir="Input_P015",
  outputdir="Output_P015",
  do.report=c(2,4,5),
  #myfun= myfun,
  windowsizes = c(60,900,3600), 
  minimumFileSizeMB = 0,
 
 
  strategy = 1,
  hrs.del.start = 1,
  hrs.del.end = 1,
 
  M5L5res = 1, 
  L5M5window= c(0,24),
  winhr = c(5,10),
 
  #maxdur = 17,
  max_calendar_days=17,
  qwindow=c(0,24),
  mvpathreshold =c(93.2),
 
  IVIS.activity.metric = 2,
  IVIS_acc_threshold= 20,
  cosinor = FALSE,
 
  
  excludefirstlast = FALSE,
  do.imp = FALSE,
 
 
  #Naps:
  possible_nap_window= c(13,18),
  possible_nap_dur= c(15,240),
 
 
 
 
  threshold.lig = c(30),
  threshold.mod = c(93.2),
  threshold.vig = c(418.3),
 
  boutcriter = 0.8,
  boutcriter.in = 0.9, 
  boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
  boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,
  LUX_day_segments = c(20, 00),
 
  boutdur.in = c(1,15),
  boutdur.lig = c(1,15),
  boutdur.mvpa = c(1,15),
  includedaycrit.part5 = 2/3,
 
 
  #=====================
  # Visual report
  #=====================
 
  timewindow = c("MM"),
  visualreport = TRUE)

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Light analysis with GGIR
parts:
Hi Antonella,

LUX per segment of the day is currently only derived for timewindow = "OO" and timewindow = "WW" and not for timewindow = "MM".

I am not sure why, and have added it to the list of things to look at, including the need to update the documentation for lux analysis.

If this is urgent for you and if you are willing to hire me to do this as part of a small consultancy project then please send me a PM.

Best,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
